data.summary: This 16‑week plan starts with the student’s weak units, interleaves new material, and ends with mixed review and timed practice. Each week is limited to 4 hours and includes concrete tasks that can be completed in one sitting. Live classes are scheduled exactly when they occur, and every unit appears at least once.
data.final_week_advice: In the last week, focus on full-length timed practice exams and quick concept reviews to solidify confidence before the AP test.

tasks: Read 1.1 and 1.5 notes; write a 200‑word summary of moles and electron configuration.
Do 10 practice problems on mole calculations and electron shell diagrams; check answers with the scoring guide.
Watch a 15‑min video on mass spectroscopy; take notes on key steps.
Solve 8 mass spec problems; annotate each step and compare with model solutions.
Create flashcards for mixture types and periodic trend facts.
Do 12 mixed‑question worksheet covering 1.4 and 1.7; self‑grade with rubric.
Draw 5 Lewis structures for common ions; explain valence electron count.
Answer 6 short‑answer questions on ionic compound formation; peer‑review with a study partner.
Attend live class; take detailed notes on instructor explanations.
After class, review notes and complete 5 class‑assigned practice problems.
Read 2.1 and 2.2; diagram bond types and potential energy curves.
Do 10 bond identification problems; record answers and rationale.
Sketch crystal lattices for ionic solids; list key properties of metals.
Solve 6 comparison questions on ionic vs metallic bonding; self‑grade.
Participate in live class; practice drawing Lewis structures and resonance forms.
Post‑class, complete 4 resonance exercises; compare with model solutions.
Create a VSEPR chart for 5 molecules; determine hybridization states.
Answer 5 hybridization multiple‑choice questions; check with answer key.
Write a paragraph explaining how forces affect solid properties.
Do 8 practice problems on predicting melting points from force types.
Derive the ideal gas equation; solve 6 sample problems with different variables.
Summarize kinetic molecular theory in 3 sentences; diagram collision theory.
Solve 5 rate‑law problems; record rate constants and units.
Perform a full stoichiometry calculation for a given reaction; show all steps.
Answer 4 calorimetry questions; calculate ΔH for each.
Explain Le Chatelier’s principle with 3 examples; calculate Q and K for a reaction.
Compute pH for a given strong acid; discuss entropy change in a chemical reaction.
Take a 60‑minute timed practice quiz covering all reviewed topics; score and analyze mistakes.
Review flashcards for each unit; spend 20 minutes on weak areas identified in the quiz.
